skill.description: Install npm packages from GitHub repositories using npm Git URLs, SSH, branches, tags, commits, and private repository authentication.
skill.summary: Guides npm installs from Git repositories, including GitHub URLs, private repository access, and troubleshooting.
skill.author: supercent-io

security_audit.summary: This documentation-focused skill is not malicious, and many backtick detections are Markdown false positives. Remaining risks include GitHub package installs, lifecycle scripts, token authentication, .npmrc edits, global binary linking, and privileged troubleshooting commands.

remediation.issue: GitHub Git installs can execute unreviewed package code and lifecycle scripts.
remediation.suggestion: Require users to verify repository trust, review package scripts, and pin tags or commit SHAs before installing, especially for global installs.

remediation.issue: Token examples place GitHub credentials in URLs or npm configuration.
remediation.suggestion: Avoid token-in-URL examples, warn about shell history and logs, and prefer least-privilege tokens or SSH with clear secret-handling guidance.

remediation.issue: The guide recommends git credential.helper store for cached credentials.
remediation.suggestion: Remove that recommendation or clearly warn that it can store credentials unencrypted; prefer OS keychain-backed helpers.

remediation.issue: Troubleshooting examples use sudo and recursive ownership changes.
remediation.suggestion: Lead with user-level npm prefixes, nvm, or local installs, and require explicit confirmation before any privileged system change.

remediation.issue: SSH key setup shows reading from the ~/.ssh directory.
remediation.suggestion: Clarify that only public .pub files may be displayed, and never ask agents to inspect private SSH keys or include key material in logs.

content.user_title: Install npm Packages from Git Repositories
content.value_statement: Teams often need packages from branches, forks, or private GitHub repositories before they reach npm. This skill explains npm Git URL formats, authentication options, install checks, and common fixes.
actual_capabilities: Explains npm install syntax for git+https, git+ssh, branch, tag, and commit references.
Shows how GitHub Git URLs can be added to package.json dependencies.
Describes private repository access with SSH keys, tokens, and .npmrc configuration.
Lists checks for global package locations, installed packages, and command binaries.
Provides troubleshooting steps for permission, Git, prepare script, cache, and update issues.
Summarizes best practices for pinned versions, lockfiles, and token handling.
limitations: It does not verify that a GitHub repository is trusted or safe to install.
It does not audit package scripts, dependencies, or released artifacts.
Private repository access still requires user-managed GitHub permissions and credentials.
Some examples use global installs and privileged commands that require careful review.

use_cases.title: Install an unreleased package version
use_cases.description: Use a branch, tag, or commit reference when a package update is not published to npm yet.

use_cases.title: Use a private GitHub package
use_cases.description: Set up SSH or token-based authentication for an internal repository dependency.

use_cases.title: Troubleshoot Git URL installs
use_cases.description: Check install paths, prepare script failures, Git availability, cache issues, and global binaries.

prompt_templates.title: Install from GitHub
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: choose the correct npm Git URL format.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me install an npm package from a GitHub repository. Ask for the owner, repo, and branch or tag before giving commands.

prompt_templates.title: Pin a Dependency
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: replace a floating branch with a safer reference.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my npm Git dependency and suggest a pinned tag or commit workflow that keeps installs reproducible.

prompt_templates.title: Set Up Private Access
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: configure authentication without exposing secrets.
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through installing an npm package from a private GitHub repository using SSH or token-based access.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose Install Failures
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: troubleshoot a failing Git URL package install.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me diagnose an npm Git install failure. Include checks for Git, authentication, prepare scripts, cache, and global paths.

output_examples.input: I need to install a package from a GitHub branch.
output_examples.output: The assistant asks for the repository and branch, recommends pinning a tag or commit for production, and gives a concise install command.

output_examples.input: My private GitHub package fails during npm install.
output_examples.output: The assistant separates authentication checks from package build checks, then suggests SSH, token, and verbose logging steps.

output_examples.input: A global Git package command is not found after install.
output_examples.output: The assistant checks the global npm prefix, package bin entry, shell PATH, and install location before changing system permissions.

best_practices: Pin production dependencies to a tag or commit instead of a moving branch.
Review repository trust, package scripts, and lockfile changes before installing from GitHub.
Use least-privilege credentials and keep tokens out of command history, logs, and package files.
anti_patterns: Do not install from unknown repositories with global permissions.
Do not place personal access tokens directly in dependency URLs.
Do not use sudo or recursive ownership changes before checking safer npm prefix options.

faq.question: Can this install packages that are not published to npm?
faq.answer: Yes. npm can install directly from GitHub repositories when the package has a valid package definition.

faq.question: Should I use a branch name in production?
faq.answer: Use a tag or commit for production. Branches can move and make builds hard to reproduce.

faq.question: Does this skill authenticate to private repositories for me?
faq.answer: No. It explains options, but users must manage SSH keys, tokens, and permissions themselves.

faq.question: Can Git URL installs run package scripts?
faq.answer: Yes. npm can run lifecycle scripts such as prepare, so review the repository before installation.

faq.question: Is global installation required?
faq.answer: No. Use local dependencies when possible, and use global installs only for trusted command line tools.

faq.question: What tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
